rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial way to say that you strongly hate someone or something.

example.jyutping: ngo5 hou2 zang1 sik6 jyun4 seoi1

rows.note: Use this shorter form when the context already makes the strong dislike clear.

example.english: I hate rainy days the most.

rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for strong hatred or hostility, especially when it is lasting or reciprocal.

example.english: There is deep hate between me and him.
example.traditional: 我同佢之間有好深嘅仇恨。
example.jyutping: ngo5 tung4 keoi5 zi1 gaan1 jau5 hou2 sam1 ge3 sau4 han6

rows.note: Use this for hatred in general when the wording is more formal or written than 仇恨.

example.jyutping: zin3 zang1 daai3 loi4 ge3 zi2 jau5 zang1 han6

rows.note: Use this colloquial noun phrase for a particular thing that someone hates, including a personal pet hate.

example.english: The thing I hate most is getting stuck in traffic in the morning.
example.traditional: 我最憎嘅嘢就係朝早塞車。
example.jyutping: ngo5 zeoi3 zang1 ge3 je5 zau6 hai6 ziu1 zou2 sak1 ce1

rows.note: Use this idiom for a person or thing regarded as a persistent nuisance and therefore especially disliked.

example.english: They cause trouble all the time, so they are really a thorn in our side—someone we hate.
example.traditional: 佢成日搞破壞，真係我哋眼中釘。
example.jyutping: keoi5 seng4 jat6 gaau2 po3 waai6 zan1 hai6 ngo5 dei6 ngaan5 zung1 deng1
